choices.text: Coalition-building was primarily a domestic political strategy to ensure bipartisan congressional support for the use of military force in the Gulf.

choices.text: Bush assembled the coalition to satisfy the War Powers Resolution's requirement that any military action be authorized by an international body before Congress could approve it.

DOCUMENT-BASED QUESTION: The Persian Gulf War and the New World Order

Directions: Read the following two primary source excerpts. Using the HIPP framework and your knowledge of US.87, write a response that analyzes both documents and constructs an argument about the Persian Gulf War's significance as a turning point in post-Cold War U.S. foreign policy.

---
DOCUMENT A
Source: President George H. W. Bush, Address Before a Joint Session of the Congress on the State of the Union, January 29, 1991 (Public domain; Public Papers of the Presidents, National Archives)

"What is at stake is more than one small country, it is a big idea — a new world order, where diverse nations are drawn together in common cause to achieve the universal aspirations of mankind: peace and security, freedom, and the rule of law. Such is a world worthy of our struggle, and worthy of our children's future... The world can therefore seize this opportunity to fulfill the long-held promise of a new world order — where brutality will go unrewarded, and aggression will meet collective resistance."

---
DOCUMENT B
Source: Joint Resolution of Congress, Authorization for Use of Military Force Against Iraq, Public Law 102-1, January 14, 1991 (Public domain; U.S. Government Publishing Office)

"The President is authorized, subject to subsection (b), to use United States Armed Forces pursuant to United Nations Security Council Resolution 678 (1990) in order to achieve implementation of Security Council Resolutions 660, 661, 662, 664, 665, 666, 667, 669, 670, 674, and 677... The President shall, at least once every 60 days, submit to the Congress a summary on the status of efforts to obtain compliance by Iraq with the resolutions adopted by the United Nations Security Council..."

---
Using both documents and your knowledge of US.87, write a response that: (1) applies HIPP to each document; (2) constructs an argument about what these documents reveal about how U.S. foreign policy authority was exercised during the Gulf War; and (3) evaluates how successfully the Gulf War achieved the 'new world order' Bush described, drawing on knowledge of subsequent events including US.91.
items.stemEs:
PREGUNTA BASADA EN DOCUMENTOS: La Guerra del Golfo Pérsico y el Nuevo Orden Mundial

Instrucciones: Lea los siguientes dos fragmentos de fuentes primarias. Usando el marco HIPP y su conocimiento de US.87, escriba una respuesta que analice ambos documentos y construya un argumento sobre el significado de la Guerra del Golfo Pérsico como un punto de inflexión en la política exterior estadounidense posterior a la Guerra Fría.

---
DOCUMENTO A
Fuente: Presidente George H. W. Bush, Discurso ante una Sesión Conjunta del Congreso sobre el Estado de la Unión, 29 de enero de 1991 (Dominio público; Documentos Públicos de los Presidentes, Archivos Nacionales)

"Lo que está en juego es más que un pequeño país, es una gran idea — un nuevo orden mundial, donde naciones diversas se unen en una causa común para lograr las aspiraciones universales de la humanidad: paz y seguridad, libertad y el estado de derecho. Tal es un mundo digno de nuestra lucha, y digno del futuro de nuestros hijos... Por lo tanto, el mundo puede aprovechar esta oportunidad para cumplir la promesa largamente esperada de un nuevo orden mundial — donde la brutalidad no será recompensada, y la agresión encontrará resistencia colectiva."

---
DOCUMENTO B
Fuente: Resolución Conjunta del Congreso, Autorización para el Uso de la Fuerza Militar Contra Irak, Ley Pública 102-1, 14 de enero de 1991 (Dominio público; Oficina de Publicaciones del Gobierno de EE. UU.)

"El Presidente está autorizado, sujeto a la subsección (b), para usar las Fuerzas Armadas de los Estados Unidos de conformidad con la Resolución 678 (1990) del Consejo de Seguridad de las Naciones Unidas para lograr la implementación de las Resoluciones 660, 661, 662, 664, 665, 666, 667, 669, 670, 674 y 677 del Consejo de Seguridad... El Presidente deberá, al menos una vez cada 60 días, presentar al Congreso un resumen sobre el estado de los esfuerzos para obtener el cumplimiento por parte de Irak de las resoluciones adoptadas por el Consejo de Seguridad de las Naciones Unidas..."

---
Usando ambos documentos y su conocimiento de US.87, escriba una respuesta que: (1) aplique HIPP a cada documento; (2) construya un argumento sobre lo que estos documentos revelan sobre cómo se ejerció la autoridad de política exterior de EE. UU. durante la Guerra del Golfo; y (3) evalúe qué tan exitosamente la Guerra del Golfo logró el 'nuevo orden mundial' que describió Bush, basándose en el conocimiento de eventos posteriores que incluyen US.91.
items.correctAnswer: A top-score response applies HIPP with precision: Document A — Historical context: the first major post-Cold War military conflict, with the Berlin Wall having fallen only 14 months earlier; Intended audience: Congress, the American public, and international allies; Purpose: to frame the Gulf War as a multilateral effort to establish a rules-based international order, not merely to defend U.S. oil interests; Point of view: Bush, a former UN Ambassador and CIA Director, with genuine belief in multilateral institutions but also aware that domestic support required idealistic framing. Document B — Historical context: Congress passing authorization one day before the UN deadline for Iraq to withdraw from Kuwait; Intended audience: the President, the military, and international observers watching whether U.S. constitutional requirements were followed; Purpose: to provide legal authorization for military force while maintaining congressional authority (contrast with the Gulf of Tonkin Resolution, US.78, which gave even broader authority with less specificity); Point of view: a Congress asserting its war powers role while accepting presidential foreign policy leadership. The argument about foreign policy authority: unlike Vietnam (US.78) where the Gulf of Tonkin Resolution gave a blank check, the Gulf War AUMF was tied specifically to UN resolutions, reflecting post-Vietnam War Powers Resolution constraints. The evaluation of the 'new world order': Bush's vision was partially realized — the Gulf War coalition successfully expelled Iraq from Kuwait and established the precedent of multilateral collective security — but the order proved fragile. Saddam Hussein remained in power, the U.S. maintained troops in Saudi Arabia (a grievance that Osama bin Laden cited as motivation for 9/11, US.90), and the 2003 invasion of Iraq (US.91) without UN authorization represented the collapse of the multilateral framework Bush had championed.
items.dokRationale: Student must synthesize across multiple standards and sources, constructing an extended argument that connects US.87, US.91 through evidence-based reasoning requiring sustained analytical writing.

SCORING GUIDE (6 points):
6 - Exemplary: Full HIPP analysis of both documents with specific, historically accurate context, audience, purpose, and point-of-view analysis. Argument clearly identifies the constitutional significance of a specific AUMF (vs. Gulf of Tonkin blank check). Evaluates 'new world order' with specific reference to subsequent events (Saddam remaining in power, Saudi bases as bin Laden grievance, 2003 Iraq War unilateralism, US.91).
5 - Advanced: HIPP applied to both documents with minor gaps. Argument addresses foreign policy authority comparison. Evaluation of 'new world order' references at least one subsequent event.
4 - Proficient: HIPP applied to both documents but some elements superficial. Argument about foreign policy authority is present. Evaluation of 'new world order' is general.
3 - Adequate: HIPP applied to one document fully. Argument about foreign policy is attempted. Some reference to subsequent events.
2 - Developing: Partial HIPP for one document. Argument about Gulf War policy is vague. No evaluation of 'new world order' outcomes.
